public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source support that outcome value and timing can be coupled and that the delayed-outcome filtration matters; used to motivate explicit separation of physical completion from statistical reveal.

public_sources.title: Towards Multi-Model LLM Schedulers: Empirical Insights into Offloading and Preemption
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that LLM preemption can have substantial, hardware/model-dependent overhead dominated by state reload; motivates reporting effective cancellation savings separately from full launched obligation and resume overhead.

public_sources.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Primary-source evidence that cache-aware preemption and tail behavior materially affect serving latency; used only as systems context, not as proof of the evaluation-specific scheduler result.

pathwise_physical_scheduler_invariance.statement: Freeze an ordered paired-outcome sequence X_1,...,X_N before it becomes statistically eligible, including prompt/environment/model/seed/attempt identity. A physical scheduler may launch, delay, preempt, resume, or cancel computation and may use arbitrarily rich timing/resource history. Statistical reveal is restricted to the largest completed prefix K(t), with no skip or reorder. A hard deadline D returns unresolved unless the original timing-blind prefix test has already crossed. Then {false commit by D} is a pathwise subset of {the original no-deadline prefix test ever crosses on X_1,...,X_N}. Hence physical scheduling and informative latency cannot increase unconditional false-commit probability under these conditions.
pathwise_physical_scheduler_invariance.finite_horizon_control: For the current +1.5/-0.5 fair-sign e-process with threshold 20 and N=50, exact no-deadline null crossing probability is 0.03759043021723407, below the nominal Ville bound 0.05. Any fail-closed physical deadline preserving frozen outcome identity/order is bounded by this same crossing event.
safe_operations: independent side-slot reuse that changes only completion times
timing-aware preemption followed by resume of the same frozen attempt/output identity
cancelling unrevealed future work after a valid commit
cancelling all remaining work at a fail-closed deadline and returning unresolved
unsafe_or_uncovered_operations: completion-order statistical inclusion or skipping/reordering pairs
preempt-and-restart that draws a fresh stochastic model output and substitutes it for the frozen attempt
hedging multiple stochastic attempts and choosing the first/fastest/best attempt as the pair outcome
accept-on-timeout or timing-dependent changes to the statistical bet/boundary without a richer conditional-null proof

hedged_retry_counterexample.construction: Each attempt is null-fair: sign + or - with probability 1/2. Let + attempts finish at time 1 and - attempts at time 2. Launch two independent duplicate attempts and define the pair outcome as the first completion.
hedged_retry_counterexample.result: Observed P(+)=3/4 because the first completion is + unless both attempts are -. The current one-step e-factor then has expectation 0.75*1.5 + 0.25*0.5 = 1.25 > 1, so e-validity is destroyed even though each underlying attempt was individually fair. Fixed reveal order alone does not protect against scheduler-induced replacement of the outcome identity.
hedged_retry_counterexample.implication: Resume/cancel is statistically safe only if it preserves the same frozen attempt (or the retry policy itself is frozen before seeing timing/outcomes and the resulting composite outcome has a separately valid null).

synthetic_side_level_stress.status: Worker-local synthetic Monte Carlo and exact/pathwise reasoning only; not a deployed serving measurement.

model.latency: correlated lognormal side latencies with shared task difficulty, side noise, and independent 1% x10 side stragglers
model.sign_latency_dependence: null/alternative + pairs are globally faster and - pairs slower by reciprocal exp(+-0.35) multiplier
model.statistical_test: + factor 1.5, - factor 0.5, threshold 20, fixed covariate-blind pair order
model.deadline_origin: independent 10k-run calibration: median no-deadline pair-locked wall time under null; normalized synthetic units

policies.pairlock: 16 paired slots; both side slots reserved until slower side finishes
policies.sideW16: 32 shared side slots; only first 16 unrevealed pair indices may have work in flight
policies.sideW50: same with all 50 pair indices eligible; fixed statistical reveal still enforced

interpretation: In this simulator, unrestricted side-level reuse (W50) recovered essentially the same compute and slightly higher deadline resolution than pair-locking, while eliminating the artificial requirement to reserve both side slots until the slower side completes. Under the paired-reservation accounting model, null mean occupancy falls from 301.36 paired-slot units to about 222.49 side-compute units (~26%); this is a reservation-model comparison, not a claim about provider billing.

The wall/resolution benefit of side-level reuse was modest; its main tested benefit was avoiding stranded side-slot reservation. Bounded lookahead W16/W32 reduced launched compute but sharply lowered deadline resolution and made the resolved subset more compositionally biased.

If cancellation really stops launched work at commit/deadline, effective side compute was ~7-8% below full launched obligation for W50/pairlock in these deadline conditions. If the serving stack charges or continues already-launched work, this saving does not materialize; preemption/reload overhead must be measured separately.

All unconditional false-commit estimates remain below the exact 3.759% no-deadline crossing probability within Monte Carlo error; resolved-only false-commit fractions can be much larger under aggressive lookahead restriction because censoring is informative.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Separate statistical outcome identity/order from physical execution. Side-level reuse, preemption, and cancellation are validity-neutral only when they cannot replace or reorder the frozen paired outcomes seen by the test.

Treat preempt-and-resume and cancel-and-rerun as statistically different operations. Resume of the same deterministic/frozen attempt preserves the pathwise subset argument; rerunning a stochastic model can create a new selected outcome and needs its own null proof.

For deadline/cancellation studies report at least: unconditional false-commit probability, resolved fraction, resolved-only composition, full launched obligation, effective work under successful cancellation, and preemption/reload overhead. Do not infer compute savings from wall-time alone.

Do not tighten lookahead merely to save launched work without measuring unresolved rate and resolved-subset composition; in the tested stress W16 saved compute but reduced null resolved fraction from ~50% to ~14% and inflated false-commit share among resolved runs.

A physical scheduler may use timing/resource history, even when timing is outcome-associated, without increasing unconditional FWER if it only changes reveal times and the deadline is fail-closed. The critical prohibition is scheduler-induced selection/replacement/reordering of statistical outcomes, not timing awareness by itself.
scope_guards: All latency/occupancy figures are normalized synthetic Monte Carlo; no deployed hardware, provider, model, billing scheme, or real cancellation semantics were measured.

The ~26% reservation reduction assumes pair-locking truly reserves two side slots until the slower side completes and side-level scheduling can independently reuse freed capacity; actual GPU schedulers may have memory/KV/cache constraints and preemption costs that change the tradeoff.

The pathwise theorem controls unconditional false-commit probability only for a pre-existing valid prefix test on frozen outcomes. It does not establish power, resolved-only calibration, or validity of timing-dependent outcome generation.
The duplicate-hedging counterexample is an existence proof, not a claim that any current serving stack uses this unsafe rule.
Monte Carlo estimates have sampling error; the exact 3.759043% finite-horizon null crossing calculation and the pathwise subset relation are not Monte Carlo claims.

frontier.action: Add explicit attempt-identity semantics to the scheduler model: deterministic resume, stochastic restart, and hedged duplicate. Derive valid retry constructions that allow redundancy without first-completion selection bias, e.g. freeze a retry/aggregation rule before observing timing and test the resulting composite paired outcome.

Measure preemption/reload overhead and side-level memory/KV occupancy using public traces or a reproducible local serving trace; compare full obligation, effective cancel savings, and wall time rather than assuming cancellation is free.
Optimize lookahead/window size under a joint objective over q95 wall, unresolved rate, full/effective occupancy, and resolved-subset composition while keeping statistical reveal fixed.

For cases that intentionally use timing to choose among stochastic attempts or alter statistical order, derive a richer conditional e-process or design-based estimator in the timing filtration rather than relying on the prefix-subset theorem.

exact_next_action: Construct statistically valid redundancy for stochastic LLM evaluation: compare (a) frozen single attempt with preempt/resume, (b) predeclared duplicate aggregation that ignores completion order, and (c) unsafe first-completion hedging. Derive the paired-sign null for each, quantify power/cost under stragglers, and identify whether any completion-order-independent aggregation recovers tail-latency savings without selection bias.
